messages.subject: Re: Large values for gradient of Latent Variable Model
messages.subject_clean: Large values for gradient of Latent Variable Model
messages.body_plain:
The problem you experience occurs because it is possible to choose the outer parameters in a way such that the inner problem looks like a 4th order polynomial without the 2nd order term.
In this situation you are essentially integrating something like exp(-u^4) using the Laplace approximation. The result will be infinity, i.e. the outer optimization problem gets infinite reward by going into the bad parts of the parameter space where the Laplace approximation is inaccurate!
You'll see the negative log likelihood function has a ridge where it is most inaccurate (that's why you get the large gradients):

prof <- tmbprofile(model, 1, slice=TRUE, ytol=20)
plot(prof)

It is likely that in the future TMB will be able to handle your example using different integration techniques. For now the only easy option seems to be MCMC, e.g.:

library(tmbstan)
fit <- tmbstan(model)
plot(fit)

FWIW, another example with the same symptoms is given here: https://github.com/kaskr/laplace_accuracy

My data consists of a list of matrices with integer values.

Any one of these on their own I would pass to TMB using DATA_IMATRIX()

How can I send the whole list so that in the end TMB stores them as vector<matrix<int> >

The other way I thought to do it was to send a 3D array and slice it up in C++ but there doesn't seem to be an easy way to do that either.

Andy

messages.subject: Positive confidence intervals for data that is zero-inflated
messages.subject_clean: Positive confidence intervals for data that is zero-inflated
messages.body_plain:
I am using glmmTMB to look at the data below. Egg number is the variable I am interested and the ppb refer to a pesticide concentration.

A hurdle approach is clearly the right approach to use for this data (I am interested in both the zero/count outputs) and thus the code used is;

full_model<-glmmTMB(egg_number~treatment+(1|original_colony),data = colony_data, ziformula=~.,family=truncated_poisson)

M0<-glmmTMB(egg_number~1+(1|original_colony),data = colony_data, ziformula=~.,family=truncated_poisson)

model.sel(full_model,M0)

summary(full_model)

confint(full_model)

Everything runs fine and the results are as expected but when plotting the confidence intervals using the confint function the estimates for the zero inflated part of the model at 250ppb are positive (see below, highlighted yellow)

                                               2.5 %      97.5 %    Estimate

cond.(Intercept)                          2.79742862  3.04169246  2.91956054

cond.treatmentb.5ppb                     -0.31039812 -0.01374274 -0.16207043

cond.treatmentc.10ppb                    -0.23927447  0.04183210 -0.09872118

cond.treatmentd.250ppb                   -1.91255944 -0.69548880 -1.30402412

original_colony.cond.Std.Dev.(Intercept)  0.04105453  0.22809239  0.09676893

zi.zi~(Intercept)                        -3.02949098 -0.02523687 -1.52736392

zi.zi~treatmentb.5ppb                    -0.45068969  2.23628979  0.89280005

zi.zi~treatmentc.10ppb                   -0.88815643  1.84441758  0.47813058

zi.zi~treatmentd.250ppb                   2.81994191  6.93370741  4.87682466

original_colony.zi.Std.Dev.(Intercept)    0.69680373  3.04478442  1.45657720

Given the results (only one positive value) for 250pbb this seems odd to me, as surly you would expect it to be a negative value? I have made several mock data sets and find the same result every time. Is this something to do with how this package reads the data or should I be worried about it? Any advice of suggestions would be much appreciated!

messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Positive confidence intervals for data that is zero-inflated
messages.subject_clean: [TMB users] Positive confidence intervals for data that is zero-inflated
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

not sure if the following answers your question, but since it might, I'll write it to you anyway.

I think it is crucial to realize that the 'zero inflated' part of the model, models the probability of an 'extra' zero occurring. The higher the probability of an additional zero occurring is, the lower the expected egg-count. This should explain why higher coefficient values lead to lower expected values. In the end, the overall expected value can be calculated by multiplying the probability of not obtaining an additional zero (1 - p(zi), with p(zi)=plogis(zi.zi.intercept+zi.zi.treatment.250ppb)) with the expected outcome of the fixed effect model.

Obtaining confidence intervals for these expectations can be hard however, as also discussed in https://github.com/glmmTMB/glmmTMB/issues/378 .

Best regards,

Koen

For those curious I ran MCMC on this. I think I'm having similar issues with my own model so I wanted to look deeper into this. Several parameters are bimodal in MCMC and it's easy to see why. Since b1 is so small a value of u=2 and u=-2 will lead to the same prediction. I've attached an output plot showing the behavior. So it seems it's not a LA-specific problem, but rather an ill-posed model more generally.

messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Re: NA/NaN warning
messages.body_plain:
Hi Craig, thanks for following up. That is indeed a good tip and I just used it today. However I had something strange happen. When the model crashes with NaN gradient

Error in nlminb(start = startpar, objective = fn, gradient = gr, control = control,  :

  (converted from warning) NA/NaN function evaluation

I then pass that last.par through and as expected get NaN for both fn and gr

all <- Obj$env$last.par
fixed <- all[-Obj$env$random]
Obj$fn(fixed)
Obj$gr(fixed)

However, when I run the report and extract the objective function (jnll) it is not NaN!

> Obj$report(all)$jnll
[1] 70987.23

This NLL is about what the starting values are, i.e., not great but not outrageous. How is it possible that fn() returns NaN but report()$nll is valid? I assume there is something weird going on with the LA? When I take the trace output and put it back through the model to get a fn and max(abs(gr)) values the NLL decreases as expected but the gradients are not reliable.

I'm experimenting with MCMC but thought I'd ask if anyone else has experienced such strange behavior.

messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Re: NA/NaN warning
messages.body_plain:
Cole, the reason is that 'Obj$fn(fixed)' is the marginal likelihood obtained using the LA. LA returns NaN because the inner hessian matrix is singular (determinant=0). That's why this really is a problem with the LA: The marginal likelihood, determined by LA, becomes infinite when the outer parameters are tuned in a way such that singularity occurs. nlminb always ends up with a crazy value because it gets attracted by the worst possible point(s) in the parameter space where LA is most inaccurate!
In contrast 'Obj$report(all)$jnll' returns the joint negative log likelihood which is finite. There is no contradiction.

From: tmb-...@googlegroups.com <tmb-...@googlegroups.com> on behalf of Cole Monnahan <mon...@uw.edu>
Sent: Thursday, March 28, 2019 5:47:38 PM
To: Craig Marsh
Cc: Hans Skaug; TMB Users
Subject: Re: [TMB users] Re: NA/NaN warning

Hi Craig, thanks for following up. That is indeed a good tip and I just used it today. However I had something strange happen. When the model crashes with NaN gradient

Error in nlminb(start = startpar, objective = fn, gradient = gr, control = control,  :
  (converted from warning) NA/NaN function evaluation

I then pass that last.par through and as expected get NaN for both fn and gr

all <- Obj$env$last.par
fixed <- all[-Obj$env$random]
Obj$fn(fixed)
Obj$gr(fixed)

However, when I run the report and extract the objective function (jnll) it is not NaN!

> Obj$report(all)$jnll
[1] 70987.23

This NLL is about what the starting values are, i.e., not great but not outrageous. How is it possible that fn() returns NaN but report()$nll is valid? I assume there is something weird going on with the LA? When I take the trace output and put it back through the model to get a fn and max(abs(gr)) values the NLL decreases as expected but the gradients are not reliable.

I'm experimenting with MCMC but thought I'd ask if anyone else has experienced such strange behavior.
